sanskrit: pārṣatas tu balī rājan kṛtāstraḥ kṛtaniśramaḥ drauṇim evābhidudrāva kṛtvā mṛtyuṃ nivartanam
english: But the mighty son of Pṛṣata, O king, accomplished in arms and tireless in toil, rushed straight at the son of Droṇa, having made death itself the boundary of his turning back.

sanskrit: tato bāṇamayaṃ varṣaṃ droṇaputrasya mūrdhani avāsṛjad ameyātmā pāñcālyo rathināṃ varaḥ
english: Then the prince of the Pāñcālas, that immeasurable spirit, the best of chariot-warriors, loosed a rain of arrows upon the head of Droṇa's son.

sanskrit: taṃ drauṇiḥ samare kruddhaś chādayām āsa patribhiḥ vivyādha cainaṃ daśabhiḥ pitur vadham anusmaran
english: Enraged in the battle, the son of Droṇa veiled him with feathered shafts and pierced him with ten, remembering the slaying of his father.

sanskrit: dvābhyāṃ ca suvikṛṣṭābhyāṃ kṣurābhyāṃ dhvajakārmuke chittvā pāñcālarājasya drauṇir anyaiḥ samārdayat
english: With two well-drawn razor-headed arrows the son of Droṇa cut down the standard and the bow of the Pāñcāla king, and with others he tormented him sorely.

sanskrit: vyaśvasūtarathaṃ cainaṃ drauṇiś cakre mahāhave tasya cānucarān sarvān kruddhaḥ prācchādayac charaiḥ
english: In that great battle the son of Droṇa stripped him of horses, charioteer, and car, and in his wrath he overspread all his followers with arrows.

sanskrit: pradrudrāva tataḥ sainyaṃ pāñcālānāṃ viśāṃ pate saṃbhrāntarūpam ārtaṃ ca śaravarṣaparikṣatam
english: Then the army of the Pāñcālas broke and fled, O lord of peoples, bewildered in aspect, anguished, and mangled by the rain of arrows.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā ca vimukhān yodhān dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ ca pīḍitam śaineyo 'codayat tūrṇaṃ raṇaṃ drauṇirathaṃ prati
english: Seeing the warriors turning away and Dhṛṣṭadyumna hard pressed, the grandson of Śini swiftly urged the fight on toward the chariot of Droṇa's son.

sanskrit: aṣṭabhir niśitaiś caiva so 'śvatthāmānam ārdayat viṃśatyā punar āhatya nānārūpair amarṣaṇam vivyādha ca tathā sūtaṃ caturbhiś caturo hayān
english: With eight whetted arrows he afflicted Aśvatthāman, and striking that unforgiving warrior again with twenty of varied form, he pierced likewise the charioteer with four and the four horses each with one.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho maheṣvāso nānāliṅgair amarṣaṇaḥ yuyudhānena vai drauṇiḥ prahasan vākyam abravīt
english: Deeply pierced by those many-marked shafts of Yuyudhāna, the unforgiving mighty bowman, the son of Droṇa, laughed and spoke these words.

sanskrit: śaineyābhyavapattiṃ te jānāmy ācāryaghātinaḥ na tv enaṃ trāsyasi mayā grastam ātmānam eva ca
english: "Grandson of Śini, I know your loyalty toward the slayer of my teacher; yet you shall not rescue him from me, who is in my grasp—nor yourself either."

sanskrit: evam uktvārkaraśmyābhaṃ suparvāṇaṃ śarottamam vyasṛjat sātvate drauṇir vajraṃ vṛtre yathā hariḥ
english: So speaking, the son of Droṇa loosed at the Sātvata a peerless, well-jointed arrow bright as a sunbeam, as Indra hurled the thunderbolt at Vṛtra.

sanskrit: sa taṃ nirbhidya tenāstaḥ sāyakaḥ saśarāvaram viveśa vasudhāṃ bhittvā śvasan bilam ivoragaḥ
english: That shaft, sped by him, pierced through both the warrior and his armor, and cleaving the earth it entered her, hissing like a serpent entering its hole.

sanskrit: sa bhinnakavacaḥ śūras tottrārdita iva dvipaḥ vimucya saśaraṃ cāpaṃ bhūrivraṇaparisravaḥ
english: His armor shattered, the hero, like an elephant stung by the goad, let fall his bow with its arrow, streaming from many wounds.

sanskrit: sīdan rudhirasiktaś ca rathopastha upāviśat sūtenāpahṛtas tūrṇaṃ droṇaputrād rathāntaram
english: Sinking and drenched in blood, he sank down upon the floor of his car, and was swiftly borne by his charioteer to another chariot, away from the son of Droṇa.

sanskrit: athānyena supuṅkhena śareṇa nataparvaṇā ājaghāna bhruvor madhye dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ paraṃtapaḥ
english: Then with another well-feathered, smooth-jointed arrow that scorcher of foes struck Dhṛṣṭadyumna between the brows.

sanskrit: sa pūrvam atividdhaś ca bhṛśaṃ paścāc ca pīḍitaḥ sasāda yudhi pāñcālyo vyapāśrayata ca dhvajam
english: Already deeply pierced before and grievously afflicted thereafter, the Pāñcāla prince sank down in the battle and leaned upon his standard.

sanskrit: taṃ mattam iva siṃhena rājan kuñjaram arditam javenābhyadravañ śūrāḥ pañca pāṇḍavato rathāḥ
english: Upon him—like a rutting elephant tormented by a lion, O king—five heroic chariot-warriors of the Pāṇḍava side charged at speed.

sanskrit: kirīṭī bhīmasenaś ca vṛddhakṣatraś ca pauravaḥ yuvarājaś ca cedīnāṃ mālavaś ca sudarśanaḥ pañcabhiḥ pañcabhir bāṇair abhyaghnan sarvataḥ samam
english: The Diademed One, Bhīmasena, Vṛddhakṣatra the Paurava, the crown-prince of the Cedis, and Sudarśana the Mālava struck him together from every side, each with five arrows.

sanskrit: āśīviṣābhair viṃśadbhiḥ pañcabhiś cāpi tāñ śaraiḥ ciccheda yugapad drauṇiḥ pañcaviṃśatisāyakān
english: With twenty serpent-venom-like arrows, and with five more, the son of Droṇa cut down all at once those twenty-five shafts.

sanskrit: saptabhiś ca śitair bāṇaiḥ pauravaṃ drauṇir ārdayat mālavaṃ tribhir ekena pārthaṃ ṣaḍbhir vṛkodaram
english: With seven sharpened arrows the son of Droṇa tormented the Paurava, the Mālava with three, Pārtha with one, and Vṛkodara with six.

sanskrit: tatas te vivyadhuḥ sarve drauṇiṃ rājan mahārathāḥ yugapac ca pṛthak caiva rukmapuṅkhaiḥ śilāśitaiḥ
english: Then all those great chariot-warriors, O king, pierced the son of Droṇa, together and severally, with arrows gold-feathered and whetted on stone.

sanskrit: yuvarājas tu viṃśatyā drauṇiṃ vivyādha patriṇām pārthaś ca punar aṣṭābhis tathā sarve tribhis tribhiḥ
english: The crown-prince pierced the son of Droṇa with twenty feathered shafts, Pārtha again with eight, and all the rest each with three.

sanskrit: tato 'rjunaṃ ṣaḍbhir athājaghāna; drauṇāyanir daśabhir vāsudevam bhīmaṃ daśārdhair yuvarājaṃ caturbhir; dvābhyāṃ chittvā kārmukaṃ ca dhvajaṃ ca punaḥ pārthaṃ śaravarṣeṇa viddhvā; drauṇir ghoraṃ siṃhanādaṃ nanāda
english: Then the son of Droṇa struck Arjuna with six arrows, Vāsudeva with ten, Bhīma with five, the crown-prince with four; and having cut the prince's bow and standard with two, the son of Droṇa, piercing Pārtha again with a shower of arrows, roared a terrible lion's roar.

sanskrit: tasyāsyataḥ suniśitān pītadhārān; drauṇeḥ śarān pṛṣṭhataś cāgrataś ca dharā viyad dyauḥ pradiśo diśaś ca; channā bāṇair abhavan ghorarūpaiḥ
english: As the son of Droṇa shot his well-whetted, sharp-edged shafts behind and before, the earth, the air, the heavens, the quarters and the intermediate quarters were covered with arrows of dreadful form.

sanskrit: āsīnasya svarathaṃ tūgratejāḥ; sudarśanasyendraketuprakāśau bhujau śiraś cendrasamānavīryas; tribhiḥ śarair yugapat saṃcakarta
english: That warrior of fierce splendor, of valor equal to Indra's, with three arrows at once severed the two arms—shining like Indra's banner—and the head of Sudarśana as he sat in his own car.

sanskrit: sa pauravaṃ rathaśaktyā nihatya; chittvā rathaṃ tilaśaś cāpi bāṇaiḥ chittvāsya bāhū varacandanāktau; bhallena kāyāc chira uccakarta
english: Slaying the Paurava with a chariot-lance, and cutting his car to bits with arrows, he severed his two arms anointed with fine sandal, and with a broad-headed shaft lifted his head from his trunk.

sanskrit: yuvānam indīvaradāmavarṇaṃ; cedipriyaṃ yuvarājaṃ prahasya bāṇais tvarāvāñ jvalitāgnikalpair; viddhvā prādān mṛtyave sāśvasūtam
english: Laughing, with swift arrows like blazing fire he pierced the young crown-prince, beloved of the Cedis, dark as a wreath of blue lotuses, and gave him over to death together with his horses and charioteer.

sanskrit: tān nihatya raṇe vīro droṇaputro yudhāṃ patiḥ dadhmau pramuditaḥ śaṅkhaṃ bṛhantam aparājitaḥ
english: Having slain them in battle, the heroic son of Droṇa, that unvanquished lord of warriors, blew his great conch in his joy.

sanskrit: tataḥ sarve ca pāñcālā bhīmasenaś ca pāṇḍavaḥ dhṛṣṭadyumnarathaṃ bhītās tyaktvā saṃprādravan diśaḥ
english: Then all the Pāñcālas, and Bhīmasena the Pāṇḍava, in terror abandoned the chariot of Dhṛṣṭadyumna and fled in every direction.

sanskrit: tān prabhagnāṃs tathā drauṇiḥ pṛṣṭhato vikirañ śaraiḥ abhyavartata vegena kālavat pāṇḍuvāhinīm
english: As they broke, the son of Droṇa, scattering arrows upon their backs, bore down with speed upon the host of the Pāṇḍavas like Death himself.

sanskrit: te vadhyamānāḥ samare droṇaputreṇa kṣatriyāḥ droṇaputraṃ bhayād rājan dikṣu sarvāsu menire
english: As they were slaughtered in the battle by Droṇa's son, those warriors, O king, in their terror saw the son of Droṇa in all the quarters.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tat prabhagnaṃ balaṃ dṛṣṭvā kuntīputro dhanaṃjayaḥ nyavārayad ameyātmā droṇaputravadhepsayā
english: Saṃjaya said: Seeing that army broken, Dhanaṃjaya the son of Kuntī, that immeasurable spirit, held it back, longing to slay the son of Droṇa.

sanskrit: tatas te sainikā rājan naiva tatrāvatasthire saṃsthāpyamānā yatnena govindenārjunena ca
english: Yet those soldiers, O king, would not stand fast there, though Govinda and Arjuna strove with all their effort to rally them.

sanskrit: eka eva tu bībhatsuḥ somakāvayavaiḥ saha matsyair anyaiś ca saṃdhāya kauravaiḥ saṃnyavartata
english: But Bībhatsu alone, with the remnants of the Somakas, the Matsyas, and others, marshalled his ranks and turned back against the Kauravas.

sanskrit: tato drutam atikramya siṃhalāṅgūlaketanam savyasācī maheṣvāsam aśvatthāmānam abravīt
english: Then Savyasācin, swiftly outstripping him whose banner bore the lion's tail, spoke to the mighty bowman Aśvatthāman.

sanskrit: yā śaktir yac ca te vīryaṃ yaj jñānaṃ yac ca pauruṣam dhārtarāṣṭreṣu yā prītiḥ pradveṣo 'smāsu yaś ca te yac ca bhūyo 'sti tejas tat paramaṃ mama darśaya
english: "Whatever is your power, your valor, your knowledge and your manhood, whatever your love for the sons of Dhṛtarāṣṭra and your hatred of us, and whatever splendor still is yours—show me all of it now, to the utmost."

sanskrit: sa eva droṇahantā te darpaṃ bhetsyati pārṣataḥ kālānalasamaprakhyo dviṣatām antako yudhi samāsādaya pāñcālyaṃ māṃ cāpi sahakeśavam
english: "That very son of Pṛṣata, the slayer of Droṇa, will break your pride—he who is like the fire of doom, the ender of foes in battle. Come, then, against the Pāñcāla, and against me too, with Keśava beside me."

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca ācāryaputro mānārho balavāṃś cāpi saṃjaya prītir dhanaṃjaye cāsya priyaś cāpi sa vāsaveḥ
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: The teacher's son is worthy of honor and mighty too, Saṃjaya; he bears love toward Dhanaṃjaya, and dear is he in turn to the son of Vāsava.

sanskrit: na bhūtapūrvaṃ bībhatsor vākyaṃ paruṣam īdṛśam atha kasmāt sa kaunteyaḥ sakhāyaṃ rūkṣam abravīt
english: Never before has such harsh speech come from Bībhatsu; why, then, did the son of Kuntī speak so roughly to his friend?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca yuvarāje hate caiva vṛddhakṣatre ca paurave iṣvastravidhisaṃpanne mālave ca sudarśane
english: Saṃjaya said: When the crown-prince had been slain, and Vṛddhakṣatra the Paurava, and Sudarśana the Mālava, perfect in the rites of bow and arrow—

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumne sātyakau ca bhīme cāpi parājite yudhiṣṭhirasya tair vākyair marmaṇy api ca ghaṭṭite
english: —and when Dhṛṣṭadyumna, Sātyaki, and Bhīma had been overcome, and Yudhiṣṭhira had been struck to the quick by his words—

sanskrit: antarbhede ca saṃjāte duḥkhaṃ saṃsmṛtya ca prabho abhūtapūrvo bībhatsor duḥkhān manyur ajāyata
english: —and when a rift had opened within them, and remembering his grief, O lord, an unprecedented wrath was born of sorrow in Bībhatsu.

sanskrit: tasmād anarham aślīlam apriyaṃ drauṇim uktavān mānyam ācāryatanayaṃ rūkṣaṃ kāpuruṣo yathā
english: Therefore he spoke to the son of Droṇa words undeserved, unseemly, and unkind—to the honorable son of his teacher he spoke harshly, as a base man might.

sanskrit: evam uktaḥ śvasan krodhān maheṣvāsatamo nṛpa pārthena paruṣaṃ vākyaṃ sarvamarmaghnayā girā drauṇiś cukopa pārthāya kṛṣṇāya ca viśeṣataḥ
english: Thus addressed, O king, that foremost of mighty bowmen, hissing with wrath at Pārtha's harsh speech and at words that struck every vital part, the son of Droṇa grew enraged—against Pārtha, and against Kṛṣṇa above all.

sanskrit: sa tu yatto rathe sthitvā vāry upaspṛśya vīryavān devair api sudurdharṣam astram āgneyam ādade
english: Standing intent upon his car, the valiant one touched water in purification and took up the fiery weapon, hard to withstand even by the gods.

sanskrit: dṛśyādṛśyān arigaṇān uddiśyācāryanandanaḥ so 'bhimantrya śaraṃ dīptaṃ vidhūmam iva pāvakam sarvataḥ krodham āviśya cikṣepa paravīrahā
english: Aiming at the hosts of his foes, both seen and unseen, the teacher's son, that slayer of enemy heroes, charged a blazing arrow with mantras—like smokeless fire—and, filled with wrath on every side, hurled it forth.

sanskrit: tatas tumulam ākāśe śaravarṣam ajāyata vavuś ca śiśirā vātāḥ sūryo naiva tatāpa ca
english: Then a tumultuous rain of arrows arose in the sky; chill winds blew, and the sun gave no more heat.

sanskrit: cukruśur dānavāś cāpi dikṣu sarvāsu bhairavam rudhiraṃ cāpi varṣanto vinedus toyadāmbare
english: The Dānavas too cried out frightfully in all the quarters, and raining down blood, they roared amid the rain-clouded sky.

sanskrit: pakṣiṇaḥ paśavo gāvo munayaś cāpi suvratāḥ paramaṃ prayatātmāno na śāntim upalebhire
english: Birds, beasts, and cattle, and even the sages of holy vows, though most self-restrained in spirit, could find no peace.

sanskrit: bhrāntasarvamahābhūtam āvarjitadivākaram trailokyam abhisaṃtaptaṃ jvarāviṣṭam ivāturam
english: All the great elements were thrown into disorder, the maker of day was overturned, and the three worlds were scorched, stricken as if seized by a burning fever.

sanskrit: śaratejo 'bhisaṃtaptā nāgā bhūmiśayās tathā niḥśvasantaḥ samutpetus tejo ghoraṃ mumukṣavaḥ
english: Scorched by the heat of the arrows, the serpents that dwell beneath the earth rose up hissing, eager to discharge their dreadful venom.

sanskrit: jalajāni ca sattvāni dahyamānāni bhārata na śāntim upajagmur hi tapyamānair jalāśayaiḥ
english: And the creatures of the waters, scorched, O descendant of Bharata, found no relief, for the very pools that held them were burning.

sanskrit: diśaḥ khaṃ pradiśaś caiva bhuvaṃ ca śaravṛṣṭayaḥ uccāvacā nipetur vai garuḍānilaraṃhasaḥ
english: Upon the quarters and the sky, the intermediate quarters and the earth, showers of arrows great and small fell down with the speed of Garuḍa and the wind.

sanskrit: taiḥ śarair droṇaputrasya vajravegasamāhitaiḥ pradagdhāḥ śatravaḥ petur agnidagdhā iva drumāḥ
english: By those arrows of Droṇa's son, sped with the force of the thunderbolt, the foes were burned and fell like trees consumed by fire.

sanskrit: dahyamānā mahānāgāḥ petur urvyāṃ samantataḥ nadanto bhairavān nādāñ jaladopamanisvanān
english: Great elephants, blazing, fell upon the earth on every side, bellowing fearful cries that rumbled like rain-clouds.

sanskrit: apare pradrutās tatra dahyamānā mahāgajāḥ tresus tathāpare ghore vane dāvāgnisaṃvṛtāḥ
english: Other great elephants there, ablaze, fled away, and yet others trembled, like beasts ringed about by a forest fire in a dreadful wood.

sanskrit: drumāṇāṃ śikharāṇīva dāvadagdhāni māriṣa aśvavṛndāny adṛśyanta rathavṛndāni cābhibho apatanta rathaughāś ca tatra tatra sahasraśaḥ
english: Like the crowns of trees seared by a forest blaze, O honored one, the troops of horses and the masses of chariots appeared, O lord; and floods of chariots fell here and there by the thousands.

sanskrit: tat sainyaṃ bhagavān agnir dadāha yudhi bhārata yugānte sarvabhūtāni saṃvartaka ivānalaḥ
english: That army the lord Agni burned in the battle, O descendant of Bharata, as the all-dissolving fire consumes every being at the end of an age.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā tu pāṇḍavīṃ senāṃ dahyamānāṃ mahāhave prahṛṣṭās tāvakā rājan siṃhanādān vinedire
english: But seeing the Pāṇḍava host burning in that great battle, your men, O king, rejoiced and let forth lion-roars.

sanskrit: tatas tūryasahasrāṇi nānāliṅgāni bhārata tūrṇam ājaghnire hṛṣṭās tāvakā jitakāśinaḥ
english: Then your men, O descendant of Bharata, exulting and wearing the look of victory, joyfully struck up a thousand instruments of many kinds at once.

sanskrit: kṛtsnā hy akṣauhiṇī rājan savyasācī ca pāṇḍavaḥ tamasā saṃvṛte loke nādṛśyata mahāhave
english: As the world was wrapped in darkness, an entire akṣauhiṇī, O king, and Savyasācin the Pāṇḍava, could no longer be seen in that great battle.

sanskrit: naiva nas tādṛśaṃ rājan dṛṣṭapūrvaṃ na ca śrutam yādṛśaṃ droṇaputreṇa sṛṣṭam astram amarṣiṇā
english: Never had we seen or even heard, O king, of such a weapon as the unforgiving son of Droṇa let loose.

sanskrit: arjunas tu mahārāja brāhmam astram udairayat sarvāstrapratighātāya vihitaṃ padmayoninā
english: But Arjuna, O great king, raised up the Brāhma weapon, ordained by the Lotus-born to counter every other weapon.

sanskrit: tato muhūrtād iva tat tamo vyupaśaśāma ha pravavau cānilaḥ śīto diśaś ca vimalābhavan
english: Then within a moment that darkness was stilled; a cool wind blew, and the quarters grew clear.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutam apaśyāma kṛtsnām akṣauhiṇīṃ hatām anabhijñeyarūpāṃ ca pradagdhām astramāyayā
english: There we beheld a marvel: an entire akṣauhiṇī slain, its forms past recognition, burned utterly by the magic of that weapon.

sanskrit: tato vīrau maheṣvāsau vimuktau keśavārjunau sahitau saṃpradṛśyetāṃ nabhasīva tamonudau
english: Then the two heroes, the mighty bowmen Keśava and Arjuna, delivered unscathed, appeared together like the dispellers of darkness in the sky.

sanskrit: sapatākadhvajahayaḥ sānukarṣavarāyudhaḥ prababhau sa ratho muktas tāvakānāṃ bhayaṃkaraḥ
english: With its pennants, standard, and horses, with its axle-pole and its excellent weapons, that delivered chariot shone forth, a terror to your men.

sanskrit: tataḥ kilakilāśabdaḥ śaṅkhabherīravaiḥ saha pāṇḍavānāṃ prahṛṣṭānāṃ kṣaṇena samajāyata
english: Then in an instant a glad uproar arose from the rejoicing Pāṇḍavas, mingled with the blare of conches and drums.

sanskrit: hatāv iti tayor āsīt senayor ubhayor matiḥ tarasābhyāgatau dṛṣṭvā vimuktau keśavārjunau
english: "The two are slain"—such had been the thought of both the armies, until they saw Keśava and Arjuna come on swiftly, delivered and unharmed.

sanskrit: tāv akṣatau pramuditau dadhmatur vārijottamau dṛṣṭvā pramuditān pārthāṃs tvadīyā vyathitābhavan
english: Unhurt and joyful, the two blew their finest of conches; and seeing the sons of Pṛthā so glad, your men were thrown into distress.

sanskrit: vimuktau ca mahātmānau dṛṣṭvā drauṇiḥ suduḥkhitaḥ muhūrtaṃ cintayām āsa kiṃ tv etad iti māriṣa
english: Seeing those two great-souled ones delivered, the son of Droṇa, sorely grieved, pondered for a moment, "What is this, then?" O honored one.

sanskrit: cintayitvā tu rājendra dhyānaśokaparāyaṇaḥ niḥśvasan dīrgham uṣṇaṃ ca vimanāś cābhavat tadā
english: Having pondered, O lord of kings, given over to brooding and grief, sighing long and hot, he then grew downcast in heart.

sanskrit: tato drauṇir dhanur nyasya rathāt praskandya vegitaḥ dhig dhik sarvam idaṃ mithyety uktvā saṃprādravad raṇāt
english: Then the son of Droṇa laid down his bow and leapt in haste from his car, and crying, "Shame, shame! all this is in vain," he fled from the battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ snigdhāmbudābhāsaṃ vedavyāsam akalmaṣam āvāsaṃ ca sarasvatyāḥ sa vai vyāsaṃ dadarśa ha
english: Then, by the dwelling of Sarasvatī, he beheld Veda-Vyāsa, stainless, with the sheen of a glistening rain-cloud—Vyāsa himself he saw.

sanskrit: taṃ drauṇir agrato dṛṣṭvā sthitaṃ kurukulodvaha sannakaṇṭho 'bravīd vākyam abhivādya sudīnavat
english: Seeing him standing before him, O upholder of the Kuru line, the son of Droṇa, his throat choked, saluted him and spoke most piteously.

sanskrit: bho bho māyā yadṛcchā vā na vidmaḥ kim idaṃ bhavet astraṃ tv idaṃ kathaṃ mithyā mama kaś ca vyatikramaḥ
english: "O sir, O sir, is it illusion, or mere chance? I know not what this may be. How has this weapon of mine come to nothing? And what was my transgression?"

sanskrit: adharottaram etad vā lokānāṃ vā parābhavaḥ yad imau jīvataḥ kṛṣṇau kālo hi duratikramaḥ
english: "Is this the world turned upside down, or the undoing of the worlds, that these two Kṛṣṇas yet live? For Time, indeed, is hard to overpass."

sanskrit: nāsurāmaragandharvā na piśācā na rākṣasāḥ na sarpayakṣapatagā na manuṣyāḥ kathaṃ cana
english: "Not Asuras, gods, or Gandharvas, not Piśācas, not Rākṣasas, not serpents, Yakṣas, or birds, nor men in any wise—"

sanskrit: utsahante 'nyathā kartum etad astraṃ mayeritam tad idaṃ kevalaṃ hatvā yuktām akṣauhiṇīṃ jvalat
english: "—are able to make otherwise this weapon launched by me. Yet here it has slain only a single arrayed akṣauhiṇī, blazing as it went."

sanskrit: kenemau martyadharmāṇau nāvadhīt keśavārjunau etat prabrūhi bhagavan mayā pṛṣṭo yathātatham
english: "By what cause did it not slay these two, Keśava and Arjuna, who share the nature of mortals? Declare this to me, O blessed one, asked by me, even as it truly is."
